summary.intent: Add a resolution note to a completed TODO file tracking GitHub Actions Node.js 24 updates before a June deadline.
summary.outcome: The resolution note was successfully committed after an initial amend was required — lint-staged had stashed the unstaged edit, causing the first commit to capture only the file rename with 0 insertions/deletions.

repo: Completed TODOs are tracked as markdown files under .planning/todos/completed/ and pending ones under .planning/todos/pending/ — completion is represented by moving the file between directories.
There is a Node.js 24 upgrade deadline tied to GitHub Actions, tracked via a TODO dated 2026-03-30.
workflow: lint-staged can stash unstaged changes before running hooks, meaning an edit made after staging will not be included in the commit even if it is in the working tree — always stage all intended edits before committing.

After a commit shows '0 insertions, 0 deletions', verify the committed content with git show rather than assuming the edit landed — the working tree and the commit can diverge silently in this scenario.
Amending the commit (git commit --amend) is the correct recovery path when lint-staged stashing causes an incomplete commit.

friction: lint-staged stashed an unstaged edit, silently excluding it from the commit and producing a misleading '0 insertions, 0 deletions' summary that required investigation and an amend.
